channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Moscow Hotel Manager Sentenced to Three Years for Housing Crocus Attack Convicts
item.description: A Moscow hotel manager has been sentenced to three years in prison for providing accommodation to two individuals convicted in the Crocus attack. The court delivered the verdict, resulting in the manager's imprisonment.

item.title: Uzbekistan Prioritizes Preventing Domestic Violence and Protecting Women's Rights
item.description: A meeting in Uzbekistan's Andijan region focused on preventing family-related offenses and protecting women's rights. Measures discussed include supporting women, enhancing their participation in public life, and preventing human trafficking and violence.

item.title: Direct Flights to Launch Between Kulob and Kazan
item.description: Direct flights will be established between Kulob, Tajikistan, and Kazan, Tatarstan (Russia). Nordwind Airlines will operate the flights starting September 27, with tickets priced between 1600 and 2500 somoni one-way.

item.title: Kazakhstan Days of Medicine in Kyrgyzstan: 1,300 People Examined, Memoranda Signed
item.description: The Days of Kazakhstan Medicine in Kyrgyzstan concluded with over 1,300 people examined and several memoranda signed. Leading specialists from both countries conducted joint operations, consultations, and master classes. Mobile medical complexes provided services in the Chuy region, examining 1,300 residents.

item.title: Dushanbe Hosts SCO Meeting on Competition Policy Among Member States
item.description: Antimonopoly authorities from Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) member states convened in Dushanbe to discuss competition policy. Participants highlighted the importance of fair competition, especially in the digital economy, and shared experiences in improving antitrust regulation.

item.title: UN Report: Gender Equality Will Take Over 170 Years at Current Pace
item.description: A new UN report indicates that achieving gender equality will require 171 years at the current rate of progress. By 2030, none of the Sustainable Development Goal 5 targets will be met if trends continue. Women face significant barriers in political and economic participation.

item.title: Dushanbe to Host Asian Parliamentary Assembly Standing Committee Meeting
item.description: Dushanbe will host the next meeting of the Standing Committee on Social and Cultural Affairs of the Asian Parliamentary Assembly from September 24-27, 2026. The meeting, led by Tajikistan, will be the first APA session held in the country and aims to foster cooperation and cultural exchange.

item.title: Uzbekistan and Japan discuss cooperation in training, employment, and investment
item.description: Uzbekistan's Foreign Minister met with the president of 'Onodera User Run' in Tokyo to discuss supporting employment projects for Uzbek citizens in Japan. They also explored creating new educational centers in Uzbekistan and expanding vocational training for youth. Uzbekistan and Japan aim to enhance cooperation in human capital development, employment, and investment.

item.title: Tajikistan discusses specialist training domestically and abroad
item.description: A meeting on specialist training within Tajikistan and abroad was held at the Ministry of Education and Science. Deputy Prime Minister Dilrabo Mansuri emphasized the importance of coordinating efforts and utilizing existing opportunities for developing socio-economic sectors. The meeting focused on improving selection mechanisms for overseas study and aligning specialties with national development needs.

item.title: Migrant arrivals in Europe decrease, but sea route fatalities rise
item.description: The International Organization for Migration reported a 39 percent drop in migrant arrivals to Europe by sea this year. However, the number of deaths and disappearances on these routes has increased, with over 2,300 people lost compared to 2,000 last year. The central Mediterranean route saw the sharpest decline in arrivals but a rise in fatalities.

item.title: European Commission proposes banning social media for children under 13
item.description: The European Commission has proposed the EU Kids Act to enhance online child safety, suggesting a ban on social media for children under 13. Children aged 13-15 could use platforms via 'mini-accounts' with parental controls. The act also imposes obligations on online services to prevent addictive features and limit screen time.

item.title: Tajikistan's Finance Minister discusses new financing mechanisms with Rothschild & Co
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Finance met with a representative from Rothschild & Co in London to discuss cooperation on issuing government bonds and utilizing new financing mechanisms for priority projects. The meeting also focused on improving Tajikistan's international credit ratings and exploring prospects for bilateral cooperation.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Offer 30% Tuition Discount for Children of Educators
item.description: Starting from the 2026/2027 academic year, Uzbekistan will provide a 30% discount on tuition fees for children of educators enrolled in state higher education institutions. This applies to full-time undergraduate programs. The discount is not applicable to military, foreign, non-state, or joint programs. Applications will be processed through the kontrakt.edu.uz system.

item.title: Tajikistan Explains to ICC Why Vladimir Putin Was Not Arrested
item.description: The government of Tajikistan has responded to the International Criminal Court (ICC) regarding its failure to arrest Russian President Vladimir Putin during his visit to the country. The response details the reasons behind Tajikistan's decision not to detain Putin, who is subject to an ICC arrest warrant.

item.title: Migrant Arrivals in Europe Decrease by 39%, While Fatalities Rise
item.description: The number of migrants arriving in Europe by sea has fallen by 39% this year, according to the International Organization for Migration (IOM). Despite the decrease in arrivals, the number of deaths and disappearances at sea has increased. The Mediterranean routes remain perilous, with significant increases in fatalities reported on the Central and Eastern Mediterranean routes.

item.title: Tajikistan's Pamir petroglyphs and historical sites added to UNESCO tentative list
item.description: Five complexes of petroglyphs in Tajikistan's Gorno-Badakhshan region and four historical-natural sites in Khatlon region have been inscribed on UNESCO's tentative list. The Agency for Protection of Historical and Cultural Heritage stated these sites are valuable examples of Tajikistan's heritage, significant for studying ancient civilizations and regional development.

item.title: Poland's PM Tusk warns of Russian hybrid drone and missile attacks on NATO states
item.description: Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk, citing intelligence, warned NATO states of planned hybrid drone and missile attacks by Russia. He also indicated that six major Ukrainian cities could face attacks in the coming days. The warning comes amid heightened tensions.

item.title: UN mission finds US responsible for war crimes in Iran, Tehran for crimes against humanity
item.description: A UN fact-finding mission concluded there are sufficient grounds to believe the US was behind two military strikes on an Iranian school and sports complex, deeming them war crimes. The mission also found Iran's government committed crimes against humanity during its violent crackdown on protests.

item.title: Karakol faces 80% water supply cut due to main pipeline breakdown
item.description: Drinking water supply in Karakol has been reduced by 80 percent due to a breakdown in the central water pipeline, the City Hall reported. Repairs are underway, with restoration expected by evening, depending on progress.

item.title: China ready to deepen ASEAN cooperation in digital economy, AI, and green sectors
item.description: Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang stated China is ready to deepen cooperation with ASEAN in the digital economy, artificial intelligence, and green industries. He proposed focusing on enhancing openness, expanding trade, and strengthening supply chains.

item.title: Tajikistan and China to Expand Cooperation in Potato Cultivation
item.description: Tajikistan's Academy of Agricultural Sciences and China's 'For Future Tech Group' signed a memorandum to develop long-term cooperation in potato cultivation. The agreement includes scientific research, modern technology implementation, seed production, storage, processing, and sales. Joint scientific-production and investment projects are also planned.

item.title: Tajikistan and China Discuss New Infrastructure Projects and Economic Cooperation
item.description: Tajikistan and China held a meeting on September 18, 2026, in Dushanbe to discuss economic cooperation, investment attraction, and industrial, energy, and transport sector interactions. Special attention was given to developing production chains and implementing new water-energy and road-transport infrastructure projects.

item.title: Uzbekistan Central Bank Plans to Diversify Reserve Assets Beyond US Bonds
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank plans to gradually expand its international reserve assets beyond US government bonds. As of early September, reserves included approximately 439 tons of gold, valued at nearly $65 billion, constituting about 90% of total reserves.

item.title: Tajikistan's Water Resources Declining, WMO Report Indicates Lower Reservoir Inflows in 2025
item.description: Tajikistan's water resources are diminishing, according to a new World Meteorological Organization report. Inflows into the country's reservoirs are projected to be below average in 2025. The report details the situation and its implications.

item.title: SCO trade ministers meet in Dushanbe to discuss economic cooperation and trade
item.description: Dushanbe hosted the 25th meeting of ministers responsible for foreign economic and trade activities of SCO member states on September 17, 2026. Tajik Minister of Economic Development and Trade Abdurahmonzoda Safarali chaired the meeting. Discussions focused on enhancing economic cooperation, increasing mutual trade, energy security, and investment.

item.title: Ombudsman's office helps children of labor migrants resume education in Batken region
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ombudsman's office intervened to ensure three children of returning labor migrants could continue their education in Kyzyl-Kiya. The children were initially denied admission to a Russian-language school due to overcrowding. The Ombudsman's office contacted local authorities, and the children were subsequently placed in another school.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's cabinet head provides apartment to family of deceased rescuer
item.description: The head of Kyrgyzstan's cabinet, Adylbek Kasymaliev, met with the wife of deceased EMERCOM lieutenant Askar Kazybekov, who died in the line of duty. Kasymaliev expressed condolences and assured the family of state support. Kazybekov was posthumously awarded the "Erdik" medal for bravery.

item.title: Schoolboy dies after fight between students in Kyrgyzstan's Suzak district
item.description: A 10th-grade student died from injuries sustained during a conflict with 11th-grade students in Zhygach-Korgon village, Suzak district. Two teenagers, aged 17 and 18, have been detained on suspicion of inflicting grievous bodily harm. A criminal case has been initiated, and the investigation is ongoing.

item.title: CIS exchange representatives discuss development of commodity and financial markets
item.description: Representatives from CIS countries' commodity and stock exchanges met in St. Petersburg to discuss the development of exchange commodity and financial markets. Key topics included the role of exchanges in economic regulation, principles for listing goods, and mutual access to securities. Discussions also covered digital financial assets and cooperation between national exchanges.

item.title: Uzbekistan develops 'kamikaze' drone with 1500 km range
item.description: Uzbekistan has developed a 'kamikaze' drone capable of flying up to 1500 km, presented as an alternative to the 'Shahed' drone. The drone, belonging to a private company, debuted at a defense technology exhibition in South Africa, where Uzbekistan is the sole participant from Central Asia showcasing various military products.

item.title: Schoolboy dies in Suzak district after conflict between 10th and 11th graders
item.description: A schoolboy has died in the village of Zhygach-Korgon, Suzak district, following a conflict between 10th and 11th-grade students. The 10th-grader sustained severe injuries and died en route to the hospital. Two teenagers have been detained.

item.title: Tajikistan and LONGi Discuss Solar Power Plant Construction
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Energy and Water Resources met with representatives from China's LONGi company to discuss energy sector cooperation. Particular attention was given to attracting investments for building solar power plants in Tajikistan.

item.title: Uzbekistan Central Bank to Maintain Tight Monetary Policy Until Inflation Reaches 5%
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank intends to maintain strict monetary conditions until inflation stabilizes and approaches the target of 5%. Central Bank Chairman Timur Ishmetov stated that inflation has decreased from approximately 20% in 2018 to 6.2%. The bank projects inflation to be around 6.5% by the end of 2026 and reach the 5% target next year. The main refinancing rate remains at 14%.

item.title: Uzbekistan Central Bank Considers Outsourcing Part of Foreign Reserves Management
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank plans to diversify its international reserves across asset classes, currencies, and counterparties. Central Bank Chairman Timur Ishmetov announced this at an international forum in Tashkent. As of September 1, Uzbekistan's gold and foreign exchange reserves exceeded $72 billion, covering over a year of imports. The bank also increased its gold reserves by nearly 50 tons in the first half of 2026.

item.title: Tajikistan and USA discuss bilateral relations and cooperation
item.description: Tajikistan's First Deputy Foreign Minister Farrukh Hamralizoda met with the US Chargé d'Affaires Carson Relitz Roker on September 17, 2026. They discussed bilateral relations, focusing on strengthening political dialogue and expanding economic and social cooperation. Investment, humanitarian collaboration, and the C5+1 format were also addressed.

item.title: Bishkek schools face teacher shortage, employing nearly 500 students
item.description: Bishkek schools have 274 vacant teaching positions, particularly in science and history. To address the shortage, the city is employing around 500 students under a dual education program and through agreements with universities. The number of vacancies was 527 at the end of the previous academic year.

item.title: Uzbek Mother and Three Children Rescued from Difficult Situation in Istanbul
item.description: An Uzbek woman and her three children, who were in a difficult situation in Turkey, were sent back to Uzbekistan on September 17 with the assistance of the Uzbek Consulate General in Istanbul. The mother had gone to Istanbul for work but became homeless and helpless with her children.

item.title: UN: World Prepares for Next Pandemic Amidst Emerging Threats
item.description: The international community is intensifying preparations for future pandemics following COVID-19, which caused over seven million deaths and impacted global health systems and economies. The UN highlights the increased relevance of global readiness due to new infectious diseases, climate crises, and conflicts.

item.title: Tajikistan and South Korea Sign Rail Cooperation Agreements
item.description: Tajikistan's Minister of Transport met with his South Korean counterpart to discuss strengthening bilateral cooperation in the transport sector, particularly railways. Two Memoranda of Understanding were signed, focusing on railway development, technology exchange, and educational cooperation.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces Fines and One-Year Ban for Educators Committing Child Abuse
item.description: Uzbekistan has introduced administrative liability for educators who commit violence against children during educational processes. A new law, signed by the president, imposes fines ranging from one to five basic calculation units and a one-year ban on pedagogical activities for those found guilty of physical or psychological abuse.
